ref_atoms.ref_content: KEYMGR.SIDELOAD.KMAC: Generation of keys for KMAC. The key is only visible to hardware. This is tracked in KMAC as KMAC.KEY.SIDELOAD.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies sideload key generation for KMAC and hardware-only visibility.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KEYMGR.SIDELOAD.AES: Generation of keys for AES. The key is only visible to hardware.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Sideload key generation for AES with hardware-only access.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KEYMGR.SIDELOAD.OTBN: Generation of keys for KMAC. The key is only visible to hardware and OTBN code.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Sideload key generation for OTBN, visible to hardware and OTBN code.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KEYMGR.DERIVE.ATTESTATION: DICE compliant key derivation. Used to generate attestation keys. Derived keys can be directed to registers exposed to software, or sideloaded to OTBN (KEYMGR.SIDELOAD.OTBN). 256Bit measurements can be provided to the key derivation function using a dedicated set of registers.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes DICE-compliant derivation, destination options, and measurement input.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KEYMGR.DERIVE.SEALING: Derivation of sealing keys. Derived keys can be directed to software registers, or sideloaded to hardware security blocks. 256Bit binding words can be provided to the key derivation function using a dedicated set of registers.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Sealing key derivation with destination options and binding input.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KEYMGR.GENERATE.OUTPUT: Derivation of output keys with additional salt and version. Software provided salt and version values are used as inputs in the key derivation function along with the internal key manager state. The derived keys can be directed to software registers, or sideloaded to hardware security blocks.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Output key generation using salt/version, destination options.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KEYMGR.GENERATE.IDENTITY: Derivation of output keys to software registers. Unlike KEYMGR.GENERATE.OUTPUT, the key derivation function does not support salt or version inputs.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Identity output derivation without salt/version, output to software registers.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KEYMGR.KEY_VERSIONING: The maximum version value supported by KEYMGR.GENERATE.OUTPUT is configurable via a set of write-lockable registers. KEYMGR.GENERATE.OUTPUT will fail to derive a key with a version greater than the version set in the write lockable register for any given key manager internal state.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes hardware enforcement of max version for key generation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: BUS.INTEGRITY: End-to-end bus integrity scheme.
CONFIG.SHADOW: Various critical registers are shadowed: including operation control, reseed interval, and key max version (creator, owner intermediate, owner).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Identifies specific shadowed registers (operation control, reseed interval, key max version).

ref_atoms.ref_content: OP.CONFIG.REGWEN: Various controls locked during the duration of an operation: including operation start, operation control, sideload clear, salt and key version.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies controls locked during operation (operation start, control, sideload clear, salt, key version).

ref_atoms.ref_content: RESEED.CONFIG.REGWEN: Reseed interval is software lockable.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Indicates reseed interval can be locked by software.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SW_BINDING.CONFIG.REGWEN: Software binding is lockable by software in each stage. When keymgr successfully advances, the lock is released to allow the next stage the freedom to program.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes per-stage locking/unlocking of software binding on advance.

ref_atoms.ref_content: MAX_KEY_VER.CONFIG.REGWEN: Max key version is software lockable.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Indicates max key version register is lockable by software.

ref_atoms.ref_content: LC_CTRL.INTERSIG.MUBI: Life cycle control signal is multibit.
CONSTANTS.CONSISTENCY: Basic consistency checks (all 0's or all 1's) for keymgr diversification constants.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies consistency check for diversification constants against all-0/all-1.

ref_atoms.ref_content: INTERSIG.CONSISTENCY: Basic consistency checks (all 0's or all 1's) for otp diversification inputs.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Check against all-0/all-1 for OTP diversification inputs.

ref_atoms.ref_content: HW.KEY.SW_NOACCESS: Sideload keys are not directly accessible by software.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines hardware-only access for sideload keys.

ref_atoms.ref_content: OUTPUT_KEYS.CTRL.REDUN: Software and sideload keys are redundantly controlled. Each generate operation creates a valid and a data enable (software and sideload specific). In order for a key to be populated into the software register, both the software valid and the software data enable must be asserted. The same is true for sideload. This makes it more difficult for an attack to fault a sideload key into the software key slot. An attacker would need to fault both the software valid and the software data enable. During a sideload operation, if an attacker manages to fault the valid but not the data enable, the software key is populated with random data. If an attacker manages to fault the data enable but not the valid, then the software key retains its previous value.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes redundant control with valid and data enable signals for software and sideload keys.

ref_atoms.ref_content: CTRL.FSM.SPARSE: Main control fsm is sparsely encoded.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Main control FSM uses sparse encoding.

ref_atoms.ref_content: DATA.FSM.SPARSE: Control data fsm (for redundant data control) is sparsely encoded.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Redundant data control FSM uses sparse encoding.

ref_atoms.ref_content: CTRL.FSM.LOCAL_ESC: Main control fsm locally escalates based on any detected fault in keymgr. When a fault is detected (sync or async) the fsm transitions to invalid state to prevent further legal operations from executing.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: FSM transitions to invalid state on any detected fault.

ref_atoms.ref_content: CTRL.FSM.CONSISTENCY: Main and operational fsm transitions are consistent with software commands.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: FSM transitions are checked for consistency with software commands.

ref_atoms.ref_content: CTRL.FSM.GLOBAL_ESC: When the system globally escalates, the main control fsm also transitions to invalid state to prevent further legal operations from executing.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Global escalation forces control FSM to invalid state.

ref_atoms.ref_content: CTRL.CTR.REDUN: Primary count is duplicated.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Primary counter is duplicated for redundancy.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KMAC_IF.FSM.SPARSE: kmac interface fsm is sparsely encoded.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: KMAC interface FSM uses sparse encoding.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KMAC_IF.CTR.REDUN: Primary count uses cross count.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: KMAC interface primary counter uses cross-count redundancy.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KMAC_IF_CMD.CTRL.CONSISTENCY: One hot check for kmac interface commands. Also, command enable (adv_en, id_en, gen_en) is checked for consistency throughout the operation.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: One-hot check on commands and consistency check on enables.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KMAC_IF_DONE.CTRL.CONSISTENCY: Spurious kmac done check.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Check for spurious kmac done signals.

ref_atoms.ref_content: RESEED.CTR.REDUN: Primary count is duplicated.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Reseed primary counter is duplicated.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SIDE_LOAD_SEL.CTRL.CONSISTENCY: Sideload key slot select is checked for consistency. When a key slot is valid when it should not be, an error is triggered. The reverse case is not checked, since an invalid key cannot be used anyways.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Consistency check on sideload key slot select, error on invalid valid slot.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SIDELOAD_CTRL.FSM.SPARSE: Sideload control fsm is sparsely encoded.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Sideload control FSM uses sparse encoding.

ref_atoms.ref_content: CTRL.KEY.INTEGRITY: Internal secret key is protected with ECC.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Internal secret key uses ECC protection.

ref_atoms.ref_content: CFG_REGWEN: Key manager configuration enable. When key manager operation is started (via START), registers protected by this EN are no longer modifiable until the operation completes.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes lock behavior during operation, preventing modification of protected registers.

ref_atoms.ref_content: START: Key manager operation start. Writing the valid state (1) triggers a start; all other values are considered no operation start. The bit self-clears.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines start trigger with self-clearing behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: CONTROL_SHADOWED: Key manager operation controls (shadowed). OPERATION selects: Advance, Generate ID, Generate SW Output, Generate HW Output, Disable. CDI_SEL selects Sealing CDI or Attestation CDI for output generation. DEST_SEL selects None, AES, KMAC, or OTBN as target; OTBN HW output is 384-bit. Register is shadowed with update_err_alert 'recov_operation_err' and storage_err_alert 'fatal_fault_err'.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies all operation modes, CDI/destination selection, and shadow alert mechanisms.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SIDELOAD_CLEAR: sideload key slots clear. VAL field: 0=None (no clear), 1=AES clear, 2=KMAC clear, 3=OTBN clear, other values cause ALL sideload key slots to be continuously cleared. To stop continuous clearing, SW must toggle the clear bit again.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes selective and continuous clearing of sideload keys based on programmed value.

ref_atoms.ref_content: RESEED_INTERVAL_SHADOWED: Reseed interval for key manager entropy reseed. VAL field: number of internal PRNG updates before a reseed is requested. Register is shadowed, with update_err_alert 'recov_operation_err' and storage_err_alert 'fatal_fault_err'.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines reseed request threshold based on PRNG update count.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SW_BINDING_REGWEN: Register write enable for SOFTWARE_BINDING. This is locked by software and unlocked by hardware upon a successful advance call. Software binding resets to 1, and its value cannot be altered by software until advancement to Init state.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes software locking and hardware unlocking mechanism for binding regwen.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SEALING_SW_BINDING: Software binding input to the sealing portion of the key manager. This register is lockable (via SW_BINDING_REGWEN) and shared between key manager stages. The binding value is not secret but integrity is important. The software binding is locked by software and unlocked by hardware upon a successful advance operation.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Lockable binding register shared across stages, unlocked on advance.

ref_atoms.ref_content: ATTEST_SW_BINDING: Software binding input to the attestation portion of the key manager. Lockable (via SW_BINDING_REGWEN) and shared between stages. Locked by software and unlocked by hardware upon a successful advance operation.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Attestation binding register with same lock/unlock semantics.

ref_atoms.ref_content: MAX_CREATOR_KEY_VER_SHADOWED: Max creator key version. Any key version up to the value specified in this register is valid. Register is shadowed (update_err_alert: 'recov_operation_err', storage_err_alert: 'fatal_fault_err'), and writable only when MAX_CREATOR_KEY_VER_REGWEN is set.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines max version enforcement for creator stage.

ref_atoms.ref_content: MAX_OWNER_INT_KEY_VER_SHADOWED: Max owner intermediate key version. Any key version up to the specified value is valid. Shadowed, with regwen locking.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Enforces max version for owner intermediate stage.

ref_atoms.ref_content: MAX_OWNER_KEY_VER_SHADOWED: Max owner key version. Any key version up to the specified value is valid. Shadowed, with regwen locking.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Enforces max version for owner stage.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SW_SHARE0_OUTPUT: Key manager software output share0. When a software output operation is selected, the results of the operation are placed here by hardware. May be wiped with random value on fault.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Hardware writes operation result into this share output register.

ref_atoms.ref_content: SW_SHARE1_OUTPUT: Key manager software output share1. Similar to SHARE0, hardware places operation results here for software reading. May be wiped with random value on fault.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Second share output register updated by hardware.

ref_atoms.ref_content: WORKING_STATE: Read-only key manager working state. STATE field indicates current state: Reset, Init, Creator Root Key, Owner Intermediate Key, Owner Key, Disabled, Invalid.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Reports current key manager state, reflecting internal state machine.

ref_atoms.ref_content: OP_STATUS: Key manager status. Hardware sets status based on software initiated operations. STATUS field: Idle, WIP (work in progress), DONE_SUCCESS, DONE_ERROR. Software must explicitly clear by writing back the read value.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Hardware sets operation status; software-cleared with write-1-to-clear behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: ERR_CODE: Key manager error code. Contains both synchronous and asynchronous recoverable errors. Fields: INVALID_OP (invalid operation, synchronous), INVALID_KMAC_INPUT (synchronous), INVALID_SHADOW_UPDATE (asynchronous). Software clears by writing 1 to each bit.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Lists specific error conditions with sync/async classification.

ref_atoms.ref_content: FAULT_STATUS: Read-only fault status. Fields indicate: CMD (non-onehot kmac command, async), KMAC_FSM (invalid state, async), KMAC_DONE (unexpected done, async), KMAC_OP (kmac error, sync), KMAC_OUT (all-0/1 output, sync), REGFILE_INTG, SHADOW, CTRL_FSM_INTG, CTRL_FSM_CHK, CTRL_FSM_CNT, RESEED_CNT, SIDE_CTRL_FSM, SIDE_CTRL_SEL (sync), KEY_ECC (async).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Enumerates fault conditions with sync/async property for debug.

ref_atoms.ref_content: DEBUG: Debug information register. Fields indicate input validation failures: INVALID_CREATOR_SEED, INVALID_OWNER_SEED, INVALID_DEV_ID, INVALID_HEALTH_STATE, INVALID_KEY_VERSION, INVALID_KEY, INVALID_DIGEST. All are set when respective input fails checks during operation.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Reports input validation failures for various seeds and IDs.

ref_atoms.ref_content: sec_cm_sw_binding_config_regwen: Verify the countermeasure(s) SW_BINDING.CONFIG.REGWEN. Test that `sw_binding_regwen` gates the *_sw_binding and `sw_binding_regwen` will be cleared after a successful advance operation. X-ref'ed with `random`.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: sw_binding_regwen gates *_sw_binding registers and is cleared after a successful advance operation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: sec_cm_intersig_consistency: Verify the countermeasure(s) INTERSIG.CONSISTENCY. Test `otp diversification` input with all 0s or 1s. X-ref'ed with `invalid_hw_input`.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Test otp diversification input with all 0s or 1s.

ref_atoms.ref_content: sec_cm_hw_key_sw_noaccess: Verify the countermeasure(s) HW.KEY.SW_NOACCESS. The CSRs `sw_share*_output` are checked with expected values, which should never match to HW sideload keys.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: CSRs sw_share*_output are checked to never match HW sideload keys.

ref_atoms.ref_content: sec_cm_output_keys_ctrl_redun: Verify the countermeasure(s) OUTPUT_KEYS.CTRL.REDUN. 1. Randomly advance to a functional state and start a sideload operation. 2. Flip either data_sw_en or data_valid. 3. Read sw_share* for check: - if hw_key_sel is flipped but data_sw_en is not, it doesn't match either the previously flopped value or the sideload value. - if hw_key_sel is not flipped but data_en is, you should see the previous value.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Flip data_sw_en or data_valid to check hw_key_sel and sw_share* output consistency.

ref_atoms.ref_content: sec_cm_ctrl_fsm_consistency: Verify the countermeasure(s) CTRL.FSM.CONSISTENCY. - Set `ral.control_shadowed` to OpDisable, so that no Advance or Generate operation is selected. - Force internal `tb.dut.u_ctrl.adv_en_o` or `tb.dut.u_ctrl.gen_en_o` to 1. - Check the fatal alert is triggered and `fault_status.ctrl_fsm_chk` is set.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Force adv_en_o or gen_en_o when no operation selected, check fatal alert and fault_status.ctrl_fsm_chk.

ref_atoms.ref_content: sec_cm_kmac_if_cmd_ctrl_consistency: Verify the countermeasure(s) KMAC_IF_CMD.CTRL.CONSISTENCY. - Inject one of these faults: - Verify violation of $onehot0 property of the ctrl bits leads to a fault: - Force {u_ctrl.adv_en_o, u_ctrl.id_en_o, u_ctrl.gen_en_o} to a non-onehot and non-zero value. - Verify the modification of the ctrl bits during an active operation leads to a fault: - Start a valid operation, then force {u_ctrl.adv_en_o, u_ctrl.id_en_o, u_ctrl.gen_en_o} to a different onehot value during the operation. This simulates that an operation is flipped to another operation before it finishes. - Check the fatal alert is triggered and `fault_status.cmd` is set.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Force violation of $onehot0 property or modify ctrl bits during operation, check fatal alert and fault_status.cmd.

ref_atoms.ref_content: sec_cm_kmac_if_done_ctrl_consistency: Verify the countermeasure(s) KMAC_IF_DONE.CTRL.CONSISTENCY. - Set `kmac_data_i.done` when it's not in a valid done period. - Valid done period is between dut sending out the last data and kmac returning a response with `done`. - Check the fatal alert is triggered and `fault_status.kmac_done` is set.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Set kmac_data_i.done outside valid done period, check fatal alert and fault_status.kmac_done.

ref_atoms.ref_content: sec_cm_side_load_sel_ctrl_consistency: Verify the countermeasure(s) SIDE_LOAD_SEL.CTRL.CONSISTENCY. - Clear all sideload keys, and issue a sideload operation. - Force `u_sideload_ctrl.valids` to a different and none-zero value, so that it enables more sideload interfaces than expected. - Check the fatal alert is triggered and `fault_status.side_ctrl_sel` is set.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Force u_sideload_ctrl.valids to unexpected value, check fatal alert and fault_status.side_ctrl_sel.

ref_atoms.ref_content: sec_cm_ctrl_key_integrity: Verify the countermeasure(s) CTRL.KEY.INTEGRITY. - Flip up to 2 bits of the internal key (u_ctrl.key_state_q). - Check the fatal alert is triggered and `fault_status.key_ecc` is set.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Flip bits of u_ctrl.key_state_q, check fatal alert and fault_status.key_ecc.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Smoke test accessing a major datapath within the keymgr. Test operations (advance, gen-id and gen-sw-out) in every state. Stimulus: Go through state from StReset to StDisabled. Issue gen-id, gen-sw-output operation in each state, including invalid operations in states other than normal operating states (StCreatorRootKey, StOwnerIntKey and StOwnerRootKey). Randomize CDI_SEL and DEST_SEL. Use default/fixed values for HW/SW inputs. Checks: Check STATUS reg for each operation. Check interrupts op_done is triggered when operation is done. Check err and alert recov_operation_err are triggered after invalid operation. Check KMAC key, KMAC data and output SW data for correctness. For invalid operations, check KMAC key, KMAC data and output SW data don't match to any of saved meaningful data, which are collected from valid operations.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Points to specific registers and signals (STATUS, op_done, err, recov_operation_err) with explicit expected behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Extend from smoke to randomize all SW input data. Fully randomize SW inputs: rom_ext_desc_*, software_binding_*, salt_*, max_*_key_ver, *_key_ver_regwen. Randomize key_version any value less than max_*_key_ver, to avoid triggerring invalid_kmac_input error. Fully randomize HW inputs from flash, otp and life cycle. Randomize *sw_binding_regwen. Ensure this gates the *_sw_binding and it will be cleared after a successful advance operation. Most of other sequences are derived from this to have similar init and sequence. Stimulus and checks are the same as smoke.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies hardware gating behavior of sw_binding_regwen on *_sw_binding registers, describing a concrete mechanism.

ref_atoms.ref_content: cfg_regwen is RO reg and it gates bunch of write access of other registers, which is not tested in common CSR tests. Test command and reg access gated by cfg_regwen is ignored during operation.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes a specific register (cfg_regwen) and its write-access gating behavior during operation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Keymgr contains HW sideload interfaces to output keys for KMAC, AES, OTBN. Stimulus: Generate a keymgr output to HW sideload interface, exercising all the sideload interfaces. Randomly program any value to Sideload_clear after any operation. Checks: Verify the sideload data and status for correctness.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Names specific sideload interfaces (KMAC, AES, OTBN) and the Sideload_clear register with explicit checking of sideload data and status.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Directly go to StDisabled from any state and check StDisabled is entered correctly.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies a state transition (to StDisabled) and a verification of correct entry.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Life cycle can disable keymgr and let keymgr wipe secret immediately. Stimulus: Test life cycle disables keymgr in any state. Checks: If keymgr is not initialized, check it can't be initialized until life cycle enables keymgr. If keymgr is in a valid state after StReset, key output to KMAC is wiped immediately and SW output will be invalid after OP is done. If keymgr in disabled state, check the behavior is consistent with normal behavior.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes LC disable effect on key output to KMAC and SW output, with specific checks on initialization and state handling.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify keymgr behavior on error response received from KMAC after sending data to it. Stimulus: Drive error from KMAC interface when VALID is high. Or drive all 0s or 1s as KMAC input digest data. Checks: Same as above entry - invalid_cmd.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies error injection on KMAC interface (VALID, digest data) and its expected effect.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify keymgr behavior with invalid key version. Stimulus: Randomize KEY_VERSION and MAX_*_VER registers. Checks: when KEY_VERSION > MAX_*_VER, check interrupts err is triggered. Check alert recov_operation_err is triggered and err_code is INVALID_KMAC_INPUT. Check KMAC output key is corrupted and working state remains the same.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines a clear error condition (KEY_VERSION > MAX_*_VER) with specific effects on err, recov_operation_err, and KMAC output key corruption.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify keymgr behavior with invalid data patterns. Stimulus: Drive all 0s or 1s on any of these inputs - flash seeds, otp_key, diversification ID, Rom digest etc. Make sure all cases are covered in csr_debug_cg. Checks: Check interrupts err is triggered. Check alert recov_operation_err is triggered and err_code is INVALID_KMAC_DATA. Check SW output isn't updated and working state remains the same.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Lists specific HW inputs (flash seeds, otp_key, etc.) and the expected error code (INVALID_KMAC_DATA) and behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify keymgr behavior with invalid data patterns. Stimulus: Create sync (transactional) fault occurs followed by async (non-transactional) fault, and async fault occurs followed by sync fault. Checks: Check interrupts err is triggered. Check alert fatal_fault_err is triggered. Check fault_status is updated correctly.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Details cross-fault handling with specific signals (err, fatal_fault_err, fault_status).

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify the outcome of injecting faults to security countermeasures. Stimulus: As mentioned in prim_count_check, prim_one_hot_check and prim_fsm_check. Checks: Besides checking alert and fault_status, issue an operation after injecting faults, then ensure that op_status is failed and design enters StInvalid.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes fault injection on specific countermeasures and the resulting state transition to StInvalid with op_status failure.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The key manager in Reset state must transition to Initialized by an advance command; this transition is irreversible for the current power cycle. Until then, all other software commands are rejected.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the irreversible state transition and command gating in Reset state.

ref_atoms.ref_content: When transitioning from Reset to Initialized, random values from the entropy source are first used to populate the internal key. Then the root key from OTP, if valid, is loaded into the internal key. This ensures non-deterministic hamming delta.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the initialization sequence and the non-deterministic internal key population.

ref_atoms.ref_content: When advancing from Initialized to CreatorRootKey, a KMAC operation uses the RootKey from OTP as key. Keymgr reads the root key from OTP in a single clock cycle, requiring the OTP root key valid signal to be asserted (valid=1) at that clock cycle; otherwise the root key load is skipped. Data inputs to KMAC: HardwareRevisionSecret, ROMHash, HealthMeasurement, DeviceIdentifier, SoftwareBinding.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines the OTP root key valid check and the specific data inputs for the KMAC derivation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Advancing from CreatorRootKey to OwnerIntermediateKey invokes a KMAC operation using the previous internal key as key, and data inputs: CreatorSecret (secret seed from flash) and SoftwareBinding (first owner code). This transition is irreversible during the current power cycle.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the inputs and irreversibility of the CreatorRootKey to OwnerIntermediateKey transition.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Advancing from OwnerIntermediateKey to OwnerRootKey invokes a KMAC operation with data inputs: OwnerRootSecret (secret seed from flash) and SoftwareBinding (owner kernel code). This transition is irreversible.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the inputs and irreversibility of the OwnerIntermediateKey to OwnerRootKey transition.

ref_atoms.ref_content: An advance command from OwnerRootKey transitions the key manager to Disabled state. Upon entry, the internal key is updated with KMAC computed random values, but previously generated sideload key slots and software key slots are preserved.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the OwnerRootKey to Disabled transition and the selective key preservation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: In Disabled state, any advance or generate operation updates the outputs and keys with randomly computed values and always returns an invalid operation error. If life cycle deactivation or a fault is encountered, the key manager transitions to Invalid state.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the operational behavior and error response in Disabled state.

ref_atoms.ref_content: When key manager enters Invalid state (due to life cycle deactivation or fault), the internal key, all sideload key slots, and software keys are wiped immediately with entropy.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the complete key wiping upon Invalid entry.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If key manager is deactivated while an operation is ongoing, it begins wiping all keys with entropy immediately, waits for the current operation to complete gracefully, and then transitions to Invalid state. During the wait, keys are continuously wiped.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the graceful handling and continuous wiping during deactivation with an ongoing operation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: In Disabled state, sideload and software keys are not wiped upon entry, while in Invalid state they are wiped. If after entering Disabled, a life cycle deactivation or fault occurs, the key manager transitions to Invalid using the same wiping procedure. When a fault and a disable command collide, Invalid entry takes precedence.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the difference in key wiping and the priority of Invalid over Disabled.

ref_atoms.ref_content: The life cycle controller manages the key manager: until activated, no software commands are accepted; once activated, state transitions are allowed; upon deactivation, the key manager transitions to Invalid state.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the gating by life cycle activation and the Invalid transition on deactivation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: If a command is invalid for the current state: in Reset, the invalid command is immediately rejected; in other valid states, random dummy data is sent to KMAC but internal key, sideload key slots and software keys are not updated; in Disabled/Invalid states, internal keys are updated with random data and the operation returns an invalid operation error.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the state-dependent behavior for invalid commands.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Recoverable errors are captured in ERR_CODE register and trigger a recoverable alert; fatal errors are captured in FAULT_STATUS register and trigger a continuous fatal alert.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the registers and alert types for error categories.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Synchronous recoverable error: ERR_CODE.INVALID_OP is set when software issues an invalid operation given the current key manager state. A recoverable alert is sent and the operation completes with an error.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines the condition and register bit for invalid operation error.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Synchronous recoverable error: ERR_CODE.INVALID_KMAC_INPUT is set when software supplies invalid input (e.g., a key greater than the max version) for a key manager operation. A recoverable alert is sent.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines the condition for invalid KMAC input error.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Asynchronous recoverable error: ERR_CODE.INVALID_SHADOW_UPDATE is set when software performs an invalid sequence while trying to update a key manager shadow register. A recoverable alert is sent.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines the error for invalid shadow register update sequence.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Fatal error: one-hot command check. The command received by the KMAC interface must be one-hot and stable during a KMAC transaction. Failure sets FAULT_STATUS.CMD, generates a continuous fatal alert, and causes transition to Invalid state with internal storage wiped, and also reports ERR_CODE.INVALID_OP.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the one-hot command check mechanism and the resulting fault status, Invalid transition, and error code.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Fatal error: unexpected KMAC done. The kmac_done signal must only occur during the expected transaction window. Failure sets FAULT_STATUS.KMAC_DONE, generates a continuous fatal alert, and causes transition to Invalid state.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the KMAC done check and fault response.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Fatal error: control FSM check checks that state advancement only occurs on a legal advance operation, and that an advance or generate operation is issued to KMAC interface only if the software request matches. Failure sets FAULT_STATUS.CTRL_FSM_CHK, generates a continuous fatal alert, and causes transition to Invalid state.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the control FSM integrity check and fault response.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Fatal error: sideload select check ensures a sideload key slot is selected for update only if the original software request targeted that slot. Failure sets FAULT_STATUS.SIDE_CTRL_SEL, generates a continuous fatal alert, and causes transition to Invalid state.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the sideload select check and fault response.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Fault during initialization: while advancing from Reset, after reseeding PRNG with entropy, if not both shares of the Creator Root Key from OTP are valid, the key manager wipes secrets and transitions to Invalid state.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the OTP root key validity check during initialization and resulting Invalid transition.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Fault during idle: if a fault is observed on the regfile (shadow storage error) or the FSM (control FSM integrity error) while idle, the faults are reflected in FAULT_STATUS, the key manager transitions to Invalid state, wipes internal storage, but does not report an invalid operation.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the handling of idle faults and the absence of an invalid operation error.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Operation after Invalid: once the key manager is already in Invalid state, starting an operation does not wipe internal storage (as it is already wiped) but reports an invalid operation in ERR_CODE.INVALID_OP.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the behavior of subsequent operations in Invalid state.

ref_atoms.ref_content: For an advance operation, invalid input checks: internal key is checked for all 0's and all 1's. During Reset, both shares of Creator Root Key from OTP are checked valid. During Initialized, creator seed, device ID and health state data checked for all 0's and all 1's. During CreatorRootKey, owner seed checked for all 0's and all 1's. Other states no explicit checks.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the data validity checks for advance operations in different states.

ref_atoms.ref_content: For a generate output key operation, invalid input checks: internal key checked for all 0's and all 1's, and the key version must be less than or equal to the max key version.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines the input checks for generate output key operation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: For a generate output identity operation, invalid input checks: internal key checked for all 0's and all 1's.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines the input check for generate output identity operation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Legal operations per state: Reset – only Advance; Initialized – Disable / Advance; CreatorRootKey, OwnerIntKey, OwnerRootKey – Disable / Advance / Generate; Invalid/Disabled – none. Any illegal operation leads to invalid operation error (ERR_CODE.INVALID_OP).
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the command legality table and error result.

ref_atoms.ref_content: DICE advance operation: both Sealing CDI and Attestation CDI are advanced sequentially in two KMAC transactions. The first uses Sealing CDI internal key and SEALING_SW_BINDING; the second uses Attestation CDI internal key and ATTEST_SW_BINDING.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the dual CDI advance sequence and binding usage.

ref_atoms.ref_content: DICE generate operation: software selects the CDI source via CONTROL.CDI_SEL. Only one KMAC transaction is performed using the selected CDI internal key and its corresponding SW_BINDING.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the CDI selection mechanism for generate operation.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Software binding: the SOFTWARE_BINDING registers are shared between stages. Software sets values and locks by clearing SOFT_BINDING_EN. A successful advance call sets SOFT_BINDING_EN to 1 (unlock). An unsuccessful advance (with errors) does not unlock the binding, allowing the next stage to reuse the registers.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the lock/unlock mechanism of software binding registers.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Sideload key mux: during an operation, the internal key state is presented on the KMAC key output; at all other times, the sideloaded key value (if valid) is presented. If the sideload register has no valid key, the fallback may be invalid.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies the key output selection during and outside operations.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Sideload clearing: the SIDELOAD_CLEAR register can clear one slot at a time or all at once. When a clearing bit is enabled for a slot, that slot's value is continuously re-randomized every clock cycle. Software must disable the bit to make the last random value stable; otherwise the slot is continuously randomized, preventing sideloading an actual key.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the per-slot continuous re-randomization clearing mechanism and the stabilization requirement.

ref_atoms.ref_content: KMAC interface handshake: kmac_data_o.valid, once asserted, does not de-assert until the entire transaction is complete. The kmac_data_i.ready may be asserted at any time. The last transfer beat is indicated by kmac_data_o.last, accompanied by a byte mask kmac_data_o.strb that indicates valid bytes on the last beat; earlier beats have fully asserted strb. The KMAC output done pulse (kmac_data_i.done) must be accepted within one cycle with no back-pressure.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Defines the transaction-level protocol for the KMAC interface, including valid stickiness, last/strb semantics, and done acceptance.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Generate-output-hw: when the hardware output key option is used, the output of the KMAC invocation is stored in hardware registers (not software-visible) that directly output to symmetric primitives such as AES, KMAC, and OTBN.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the storage and routing of hardware sideload keys.
